references.text: Moses promised that the Lord would raise up a prophet like him. The question "Are you the Prophet?" in [ref:Joh 1:21|John 1:21] points back to this expectation of the promised prophet ([ref:5 Mos 18:15-18|Deut 18:15-18]).

Elijah was taken up to heaven, and an expectation arose that he would return. The question "Are you Elijah?" in [ref:Joh 1:21|John 1:21] is based on this expectation ([ref:2 Kong 2:1-11|2 Kings 2:1-11]).

The prophet Malachi predicts that God will send the prophet Elijah before the great and dreadful day of the Lord comes. This is the background for why they asked John if he was Elijah ([ref:Mal 4:5|Mal 4:5]).

The angel Gabriel said that John the Baptist would go before the Lord in the spirit and power of Elijah. Yet John himself denied being Elijah in [ref:Joh 1:21|John 1:21], which shows his humility and that he pointed away from himself ([ref:Luk 1:17|Luke 1:17]).

Jesus identified John as the Elijah who was to come ([ref:Matt 11:14|Matt 11:14]), while John himself rejected this title in [ref:Joh 1:21|John 1:21]. John likely rejected a literal identification, while Jesus spoke of a typological fulfillment.

The disciples asked Jesus about Elijah, and Jesus confirmed that Elijah had already come, and that they did to him whatever they wished – a reference to John the Baptist ([ref:Matt 17:10-13|Matt 17:10-13]).
After John denied being the Messiah, Elijah, or the Prophet, they asked him why he then baptized. The question follows directly on the denials in [ref:Joh 1:21|John 1:21] ([ref:Joh 1:25|John 1:25]).

After the feeding miracle, the people said: "This is truly the Prophet who is to come into the world." The same expectation of "the Prophet" mentioned in [ref:Joh 1:21|John 1:21] is here directed at Jesus ([ref:Joh 6:14|John 6:14]).

Some in the crowd said about Jesus: "He is truly the Prophet." The expectation of the coming Prophet from [ref:5 Mos 18:15|Deut 18:15], which John was asked about in [ref:Joh 1:21|John 1:21], was here linked to Jesus ([ref:Joh 7:40|John 7:40]).

Peter quotes Moses' promise of the Prophet whom the Lord will raise up and applies it to Jesus. The Prophet that John denied being in [ref:Joh 1:21|John 1:21] is identified here as Jesus Christ ([ref:Apg 3:22-23|Acts 3:22-23]).
